text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to add new work safely. When the work is finished, merging brings the changes back into the main branch. Before merging, teams usually open pull requests so others can review the code. This workflow keeps the project organised and reduces mistakes. It also makes teamwork easier, because several people can work at the same time without conflict. Understanding these basic ideas helps you use Git with more confidence in real projects.
